overall.summary: All nine tools implement the behaviour their descriptions advertise, and the skip/dedup logic for create_entities is accurately described. However, every mutating tool silently acquires a lock file, performs an atomic temp-file rename, fires a resource-update notification to subscribers, and serialises calls through an in-process queue—none of which is mentioned in any description—and the read tools include cross-endpoint relations and silently drop unmatched names in ways the descriptions do not specify.

startup.behaviour: Reads MEMORY_FILE_PATH environment variable to determine the graph file path
Checks for legacy memory.json and renames it to memory.jsonl if memory.jsonl does not exist (migration)
Reads package.json (one or two candidates) to resolve server version at import time
Registers resources/subscribe and resources/unsubscribe request handlers and declares the 'resources.subscribe' capability
Registers a readable MCP resource at memory://knowledge-graph exposing the full graph

Acquires exclusive lock file, reads full graph from disk, writes updated graph atomically via temp-file rename
Sends a notifications/resources/updated notification after each mutation
